# ECN-2026-020 - Change notice - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4

Reason for change
-----------------
Background: Routine maintenance reviews and recent audit findings identified inconsistent tracking of thermocouple drift on Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02). Calibration records in MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 indicated variable intervals between verifications, and operators reported uncertainty about when the next verification was due. To reduce process variability and ensure metallurgical conformance for parts processed on line P2-L4, a formal standardized calibration interval is required for the furnace thermocouples.

Rationale: Establishing a documented thermocouple calibration interval reduces risk of undetected measurement drift, improves repeatability of heat treat cycles, and aligns maintenance activity with procedural expectations referenced in SOP-P2-L4-01 and SOP-P2-L4-02. The chosen interval balances equipment reliability and workload on the maintenance team while being short enough to detect drift before it impacts product quality. --------------

Affected records include the on-equipment calibration log, the maintenance master record MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2, and any process run sheets that reference thermocouple verification status in SOP-P2-L4-01 and SOP-P2-L4-02.

Specifics: The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 55 days. All calibration events recorded for EQ-P2-L4-HT02 must reference MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 and be cross-referenced on the daily control log used by operators under SOP-P2-L4-01. Any nonconforming readings discovered during calibration must be dispositioned according to the escalation path in SOP-P2-L4-02.

Implementation
--------------
Overview: Implementation will be coordinated between Maintenance, Heat Treat Operations, and Quality. The change will be applied to the calibration scheduling system, the maintenance master record MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2, and to the procedural steps in SOP-P2-L4-01 and SOP-P2-L4-02 where calibration status is checked prior to processing.

## Scope
This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 supplied by the P1 forging cell. The document applies to the forged blank state of material grade 4340 intended for downstream machining and heat treatment. It provides background rationale for the selected characteristics, inspection method details for verification, recordkeeping requirements, and examples of disposition outcomes.

## Background and rationale
The crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 is produced for high-stress rotating applications and must meet metallurgical and dimensional characteristics that enable predictable heat treatment and machining yield. Mechanical hardness in the forged condition correlates to prior thermal processing and cooling rate; maintaining the specified hardness range ensures the material will respond to downstream heat treatment as expected. Bore accuracy is critical for fit-up and concentricity during machining operations; the specified tolerance supports effective fixture alignment. Maximum forging weight is a manufacturing constraint driven by die strength and press capacity and is included to prevent equipment overload and to ensure handling safety.

The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is 26-31 HRC. The bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is ±0.09 mm. The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is 26.9 kg.

Parts: CFW-9184-50

Scope
This document defines quality acceptance criteria and inspection methods for the crankshaft blank identified as CFW-9184-50, manufactured from steel grade 4340, produced at Plant P3. The intent is to establish mandatory material and dimensional acceptance criteria, outline the inspection methodology to demonstrate conformity, and provide a consistent process for handling nonconforming items. This specification applies to raw forged blanks prior to finish machining and heat treatment operations.

Background and rationale
Crankshaft blanks for high-cycle rotating assemblies require controlled hardness and accurate bore location to ensure final machining yield and finished-component performance. The values stated in this document reflect metallurgical and machining constraints established by design engineering. Inspectors and quality engineers must verify the stated requirements on incoming and in-process forgings to avoid downstream scrap, rework, and latent field failures. The inspection methods described favor traceable, instrumented measurements and documented records to support first article verification and routine production checks.

Requirements table
| Attribute | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Material | 4340 (as specified on part drawing) |
| Hardness range | The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is 32-38 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is ±0.02 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is 80.8 kg. |
| Surface condition | Free of forging laps, cold shuts, and separation defects that would affect machinability or structural integrity (visual and tactile inspection). |
| Traceability | Each forging must be legibly stamped or tagged with the part identifier and a batch or heat number that links to mill certificates. |

Disposition options
- Rework: Parts with conditionally correctable defects (for example, localized machining or rework that will restore bore size within ±0.02 mm) may be permitted to undergo controlled rework after written authorization from Quality. Rework must be documented and re-inspected to the same acceptance criteria, including verification of hardness within 39-42 HRC where heat or stress relief is applied.

Examples
- Example A: A forging measures a bore out-of-round such that one axis lies outside ±0.02 mm while the orthogonal axis is within ±0.02 mm. The part is segregated and evaluated for repair; if a permitted machining operation can restore the bore to within ±0.02 mm without altering hardness in relation to 39-42 HRC, rework may be authorized and the part reinspected.
- Example B: A forging weighs greater than maximum forging weight 28.0 kg. The part is nonconforming and shall be scrapped or returned to the forge for corrective action; it may not be reintroduced to production.

Question: What is the required spindle warm-up time before operating Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02), and why is it necessary?
Answer:
Background: Proper spindle thermal stabilization reduces axial and radial runout changes that cause dimensional drift during turning. The machine vendor and maintenance team validated a warm-up interval to reach thermal equilibrium of bearings, spindle housing, and drive components.
Requirement: The spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes.
Rationale: Allowing the spindle to reach thermal equilibrium minimizes part scrap and spindle bearing wear. The warm-up reduces the likelihood of mid-run compensations that introduce surface finish defects.
Example: For a production run that will run continuous turning cycles, start the warm-up immediately after initial power-up and before loading the first part. If the machine is already at operating environment equilibrium, perform the same warm-up prior to any precision job.
Records to keep: Log the operator start time and completion time in the machine start checklist and attach to the job traveler. Reference SOP-P1-L1-01 for start-up checklist format and retention requirements.

Question: What is the minimum coil cooling water flow for Machining induction billet heater #3, and how was this value determined?
Answer:
Background: Induction coils require sufficient flow to remove resistive and proximity heating from coil conductors and maintain insulation life. Flow minima are set based on thermal modeling and manufacturer coil specifications.
Requirement: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min.
Rationale: Maintaining at least this flow prevents localized overheating in coil turns and reduces the risk of dielectric breakdown in the coil insulation. This value aligns with the coil vendor test sheet and the facility hydraulic capability documented in MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3.

Q: What is the specified blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01), and why must it be followed exactly?
A: The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m. Background: proper liner bolt torque ensures even clamping of liners, preventing vibration, liner movement, and accelerated wear of wheel components. Rationale: under-torqued bolts allow relative motion that leads to fretting and fatigue; over-torqued bolts can distort liners and compromise bolt integrity. Practical example: during liner replacement, torque bolts to the specified value using a calibrated torque wrench; sequence the torque steps evenly across the liner circumference to achieve uniform seating. Revision: Rev C

Scope
- This document defines the preventive maintenance tasks, method, and acceptance criteria for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) in plant P3, line P3-L4.
- Tasks cover inspection, cleaning, wear measurement, media management, and fastener torque verification required to maintain safe and consistent blasting performance.

Background and rationale
- EQ-P3-L4-SB03 is a blast cabinet used after heat treat operations to remove scale and residue prior to downstream handling. Consistent blast energy, media condition, and wheel integrity are critical to part quality and process repeatability.
- The blast wheel liner secures the wheel assembly and maintains alignment. Fastener preload affects wheel vibration and media trajectory; improper torque leads to accelerated wear or unsafe operation. Therefore, verification of the blast wheel liner bolt torque is required.
- Shot media degrades and fines accumulate during operation. Topping up media maintains charge level and abrasive characteristics; regular intervals prevent process drift and reduce the need for corrective interventions during production.

- Calibrated torque wrench capable of reading and applying 90 N·m.
- Hand tools and socket set suitable for cabinet fasteners.
- Personal protective equipment: hearing protection, eye protection, respirator per SOP-P3-L4-02, gloves.
- Shop vacuum and non-sparking hand brush.
- Media handling container and funnel for controlled top-up.
- Inspection mirror and flashlight.
- Maintenance logbook or electronic maintenance record entry device.

Procedure
Preparation
- Lockout/tagout the isolation defined in SOP-P3-L4-02 for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 before any work. Verify energy sources are isolated per SOP-P3-L4-02 prior to opening access panels.
- Don required PPE before entry into the work area.

Inspection and cleaning
- Open the access panel to the blast wheel housing following the sequence in SB-1019 for safe access. Visually inspect the wheel, liner, and surrounding structure for cracks, unusual wear, or foreign objects.
- Remove accumulated

Inspection and cleaning
- Open the access panel to the blast wheel housing following the sequence in SB-1019 for safe access. Visually inspect the wheel, liner, and surrounding structure for cracks, unusual wear, or foreign objects.
- Remove accumulated dust and media fines from the housing and inlet areas using a shop vacuum and brush. Collect vacuumed material in the provided container for disposal or analysis per SB-1038.
- Use an inspection mirror to check wheel hub and inner surfaces not visible directly. Document any surface anomalies in the maintenance log.

Blast wheel liner bolt torque verification
- With the wheel immobilized and lockout verified, clean the threads and bolt heads of the blast wheel liner fasteners to remove dust and debris that may affect torque readings.
- Using the calibrated torque wrench, apply torque to each blast wheel liner bolt until the wrench indicates the target torque. The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 90 N·m. If any bolt does not achieve the target due to thread damage or slippage, replace the affected fastener and re-torque.
- Sequence torquing in a star pattern to ensure even clamping where applicable; consult SB-1019 for wheel removal/reinstallation detail when disassembly is required.
- Record the torque verification results in the maintenance log, noting bolt locations and any corrective actions.

Shot media management
- Check media level and condition after cleaning. Top-up media as necessary to maintain consistent blast performance. The shot media top-up interval for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 48 hours. Perform top-up at or before the specified interval during scheduled preventive rounds rather than waiting for visible depletion.
- When adding media, use the dedicated media container and funnel to minimize contamination. Avoid mixing different media grades unless validated by process engineering and documented in SB-1038.
- Collect a representative media sample for periodic analysis per SB-1038 to track degradation and contamination trends. Label and retain samples as directed.

Functional check and restart
- After maintenance tasks, verify that all access panels and guards are secured per SB-1019. Remove lockout/tagout only after all tools and personnel are clear and checks are complete.

# ECN-2026-036 Change notice - Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-SB03

Related documents: SOP-P2-L1-03, SOP-P2-L1-04, SOP-P2-L1-05

## Reason for change
This engineering change notice updates the maintenance specification for the blast wheel liner bolt tightening on Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03). Field inspection and root cause analysis of recurring liner movement identified that inconsistent bolt preload was a contributing factor to premature liner wear and unexpected wheel imbalance. The change standardizes the bolt torque requirement to ensure consistent clamping force, reduce relative motion between liner and adapter, and improve component life and shot quality.

Key drivers:
- Eliminate variable operator practice observed during service records review.
- Reduce unscheduled downtime associated with liner rework and wheel balancing.
- Align the maintenance instruction with bolted-joint best practice for this assembly.

The approved bolt torque value to be applied to the blast wheel liner bolts on EQ-P2-L1-SB03 is 50 N·m. This value supersedes any previous informal guidance and is the new controlled setting for the cabinet.

## Affected items
Primary affected equipment:
- Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03)

Affected maintenance procedures and records:
- Operation and maintenance activities in SOP-P2-L1-03, SOP-P2-L1-04, and SOP-P2-L1-05 where blast wheel liner removal or reinstallation is performed. Technicians must follow the updated torque requirement when reassembling the liner.

Affected personnel:
- Maintenance technicians assigned to P2, line P2-L1
- Shift supervisors overseeing preventive and corrective maintenance on shot blast equipment
- Quality personnel who verify wheel balance and shot pattern after liner service

Note: No changes are made to any other fasteners, sealing interfaces, or structural components beyond the blast wheel liner bolts for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 under this notice.

## Implementation
Scope
- This ECN mandates application of the specified blast wheel liner bolt torque for all maintenance events that involve liner removal and reinstallation on EQ-P2-L1-SB03.

Tools and calibration
- Use a calibrated torque wrench appropriate for the head style of the liner bolts. Calibration status must be verified before use per existing calibration program referenced in SOP-P2-L1

## Inspection method
Overview: Inspection shall consist of documented sampling and 100% checks where specified by downstream needs. Visual inspection, dimensional measurement, hardness testing, and weight verification are the primary activities. All inspections shall be logged on the work order and retained as the quality record.

1. Visual inspection
- Perform a visual examination of the forged blank for laps, cold shuts, cracks, and excessive scale. Use lighting suitable for detection of surface anomalies and compare to the acceptance criteria noted in the requirements table.
- Examples: a shallow surface seam that can be removed in machining without losing effective section may be acceptable; a through-thickness crack is not acceptable.

2. Dimensional inspection - bore
- Verify the bore diameter using a bore gauge, plug gauge, or equivalent calibrated instrument able to resolve the tolerances required for fit-up. Measurement points should include bore entry, mid-length, and exit where geometry allows.
- Record measurements on the inspection checklist and confirm each measured value lies within the bore diameter tolerance of ±0.09 mm from nominal.

3. Hardness testing
- Conduct hardness testing on the forged blank at specified locations representative of the core forging cross-sections. Use a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale and follow manufacturer procedures for indenter and load.
- Ensure surfaces are prepared to allow a valid indenter reading. Record individual readings and the location for traceability. The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is 26-31 HRC; acceptance requires all recorded readings to fall within this range.

4. Weight verification
- Weigh the forged blank using a calibrated scale and capture the value on the inspection record. The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is 26.9 kg; blanks exceeding that value must be segregated and flagged for

# FAQ-029 Engineering FAQ #29

Revision: Rev A

Q: What is the correct target billet temperature setting for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01), and why is this specific temperature used?
A: The target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. Background: this target is the process setpoint used to achieve the metallurgical state required for downstream machining and forging. Rationale: setting the heater to 1235 °C ensures the billet reaches a uniform temperature profile that supports predictable material flow and surface condition during machining. Example application: verify that billets reach and hold 1235 °C prior to transfer to the machining station; if billets do not achieve the specified temperature, follow troubleshooting steps in SOP-P1-L3-03. Records to keep: log the heater setpoint, operator confirmation that billets reached 1235 °C, and any corrective actions taken. Reference procedures: consult SB-1037 for process validation data and SOP-P1-L3-03 for in-shift operator steps.

Q: What is the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02), and what actions should be taken if the limit is approached?
A: The system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 295 bar. Background: this limit is the maximum allowable system pressure for safe operation and component life management. Rationale: operating at or below 295 bar reduces risk of hydraulic component overstress and maintains predictable press performance. Example scenario: if system pressure indications trend toward 295 bar during a production cycle, pause loading and follow the pressure-relief and inspection steps outlined in SOP-P1-L3-03. Scope
This manual defines required maintenance activities, rationale, and records for Ring Rolling induction billet heater EQ-P2-L2-IH01. It covers routine inspection, preventive maintenance, and corrective actions needed to maintain safe and reliable operation. This document is intended for maintenance technicians and engineers responsible for furnace performance and material quality. Refer to ECN-2026-012, ECN-2026-048, and SOP-P2-L2-05 for related design changes, electrical schematics, and plant operating procedures.

Background and performance target
The induction billet heater is used to bring feedstock to forming temperature prior to ring rolling. The target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 1230 °C. Maintaining uniform temperature profile and consistent coil cooling prevents premature coil degradation and ensures repeatable ring geometry. Coil cooling water must meet flow requirements to avoid coil overheating; the coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 81 L/min.

Tools and consumables
- Insulation-safe temperature probe compatible with high-temperature billet measurement as called out in SOP-P2-L2-05.

- Multimeter and clamp ammeter for electrical checks per ECN-2026-048.  
- Spanner set, insulated hand tools, lifting strap suitable for coil handling.  
- Replacement coil fasteners and insulation panels specified in ECN-2026-012.  
- Degreasing solvent and lint-free cloths for coil and connector cleaning.  
- Maintenance log forms and electronic entry device per plant document control.

Procedure
Preparation and safety
- Review SOP-P2-L2-05 and coordinate with line control before entry. Lockout and tagout all power supplies to EQ-P2-L2-IH01 and post signage at the line staging area. Verify absence of residual charge using appropriate procedures in ECN-2026-048 prior to touching exposed conductors. Wear heat-rated gloves and eye protection when working near recent heat cycles.

Visual inspection
- Inspect induction coil assembly for visible deformation, cracking, or discoloration indicative of overheating.

# MM-P3-L4-RR01 Maintenance manual - Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01

Scope
This manual provides maintenance instructions and acceptance criteria for the Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) installed on line P3-L4. It covers preventive lubrication, clamp bolt torque verification, bearings inspection, and record keeping required to support safe, repeatable operation in the heat treat cell. This document aligns with shop best practices and references related procedural documents (SB-1028, SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-03).

Background and rationale
Radial ring rolling mills in heat treat service are subject to cyclic loading, elevated ambient conditions near furnaces, and contamination from scale and quench media. Critical interfaces include the mandrel clamp and main roll bearings. The mandrel clamp bolt preload directly affects ring control and concentricity during rolling; loss of preload can produce out-of-tolerance parts and pose safety risks. Main roll bearings require a consistent lubrication cadence to preserve film thickness and prevent premature fatigue. Prescribed torque and lubrication intervals are set to maintain preload and bearing life while accommodating the mill's operating environment.

This quality specification applies to the manufacture, inspection, and disposition of the axle hub CFW-1140-78 (CFW-1140-78) forged from 4140 material in Plant P1. It defines the acceptance criteria for mechanical condition and dimensional features important to fit, function, and downstream machining. Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-HT02

## Scope
This maintenance manual section defines lubrication and fluid handling controls for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02). It covers acceptable lubricants, transfer and storage practices, fill and service procedures, and recordkeeping required to support consistent quench and handling performance during heat treatment operations. This document applies to maintenance and process technicians responsible for EQ-P2-L2-HT02 and to quality personnel performing verification audits in accordance with QS-PROC-08 and the operating sequences referenced in SOP-P2-L2-01 and SOP-P2-L2-03.

Background and rationale: improper lubrication or contaminated fluids can compromise part geometry, surface finish, and metallurgical outcomes. Controls in this document are intended to prevent cross-contamination, ensure fluid integrity during service, and preserve the defined quench characteristics necessary for process repeatability.

Note: The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 16 seconds.

The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is CFW-LUB-376.

## Tools and materials
- Clean service cart or tray dedicated to EQ-P2-L2-HT02.
- Filter-equipped transfer pump compatible with CFW-LUB-376.
- Closed-top, labeled containers for temporary holding that are dedicated to CFW-LUB-376.
- Particle and water-testing kits suitable for the lubricant formulation CFW-LUB-376.
- Personal protective equipment as required by site safety procedures and SOP-P2-L2-01.
- Clean, lint-free wipes and funnel with particulate screen.
- Seals and gasket kits approved for contact with CFW-LUB-376.
- Logbook or electronic record entry device for maintenance records, per QS-PROC-08.

All tools that contact lubricants or fluids must be cleaned and dedicated to EQ-P2-L2-HT02 or clearly marked for single-equipment use to prevent cross-contamination between lines.

Question: What triggers the dust collector alarm on the Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2, and what steps should be taken when it trips?

- Perform filter cleaning per the maintenance checklist in SB-1033.

# SB-1019 - Safety bulletin: quench oil fire risk
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-SB03

Hazard description
- Background: Recent checks of the dust collection system serving the Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) identified an elevated dust collector pressure drop alarm setpoint being reached during normal operation. The dust load on the collector can increase quench oil mist settling in downstream fabric filters and ductwork. Accumulated oil-dust deposits in the collector or downstream plenums present a combustible mixture that can be ignited by hot particulates, electrostatic discharge, or frictional heating from clogged blowers, creating a quench oil fire risk in the heat treat area.
- Observation: The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 1510 Pa. This alarm level has been confirmed by maintenance logs and transient capture during last shutdowns, indicating the collector has reached a resistance to airflow consistent with significant media loading. A sustained condition at this alarm indicates a decreased capture efficiency for oil mist and increased potential for deposit accumulation. Operators must assume the presence of oil-impregnated dust layers in the system when this alarm value is recorded.
- Step rationale: The alarm value of 1510 Pa is used as the operational trigger to prevent extended operation under high loading conditions. Allowing continued operation beyond this level increases the risk window for ignition events and reduces the ability of emergency mitigation measures to control a fire. Actions below are intended to eliminate fuel sources, interrupt ignition paths, and restore filtration performance.

Affected equipment
- Primary: Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) and its dedicated dust collector and ductwork.
- Adjacent systems: Local ventilation and plenum serving the heat treat bay, portable air handling equipment used for maintenance, and any temporary quench oil application devices that share recovery or drainage systems with EQ-P3-L4-SB03.
- Refer to documented maintenance and machine history in MM-P3-L4-SB03 for past filter change records and SB-1038 for related quench oil incident analyses. Operational steps and permitted startup sequence adjustments are detailed in SOP-P3-L4-02.

Required controls
- Immediate actions upon alarm:
  - Stop production feeds to the shot blast cabinet and place EQ-P3-L4-SB03 in safe shutdown

## Inspection method
Overview: Inspection shall consist of documented sampling and 100% checks where specified by downstream needs. Visual inspection, dimensional measurement, hardness testing, and weight verification are the primary activities. All inspections shall be logged on the work order and retained as the quality record.

1. Visual inspection
- Perform a visual examination of the forged blank for laps, cold shuts, cracks, and excessive scale. Use lighting suitable for detection of surface anomalies and compare to the acceptance criteria noted in the requirements table.
- Examples: a shallow surface seam that can be removed in machining without losing effective section may be acceptable; a through-thickness crack is not acceptable.

2. Dimensional inspection - bore
- Verify the bore diameter using a bore gauge, plug gauge, or equivalent calibrated instrument able to resolve the tolerances required for fit-up. Measurement points should include bore entry, mid-length, and exit where geometry allows.
- Record measurements on the inspection checklist and confirm each measured value lies within the bore diameter tolerance of ±0.09 mm from nominal.

Perform containment to prevent further processing of affected material. Example of hardness failure response: a single forging reads outside 28-32 HRC at two locations. The lot is quarantined; three additional forgings from the same heat are sampled. If multiple parts are out of range, halt production, notify metallurgy, and coordinate a corrective action that may include hold, rework approval, or scrap. Record decisions and supporting test data.

Example of bore tolerance failure response: if an unmachined bore is outside ±0.10 mm, perform inspection of adjacent forgings in the run. If the issue is isolated, scrap or rework per engineering discretion; if systematic, review die fit, mandrel condition, and process parameters.

This quality specification defines the acceptance criteria and inspection methods for the track link CFW-7661-91 (CFW-7661-91). It applies to forgings delivered to P1 and to all in-plant operations that affect final hardness, bore diameter, and forging weight. The intent is to ensure functional interchangeability and service life consistent with design requirements for the CFW-7661-91 family.

Requirements table
The table below lists the mandatory quality attributes and acceptance criteria for CFW-7661-91.

| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Through-hardness | 39-42 HRC | All finished inspection points must fall within 39-42 HRC |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.02 mm | Measured bores must be within nominal dimension ±0.02 mm |
| Forging weight | Maximum forging weight 28.0 kg | Any forging exceeding 28.0 kg is rejected for this part number |

Inspection method
Hardness
- Purpose: Verify through-hardness distribution meets the requirement 39-42 HRC for CFW-7661-91.
- Method: Use a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester and apply the manufacturer’s standard procedure for HRC measurement on steel forgings. Measurements shall be taken at locations representative of service-critical sections including the girth area and the bore collar. For each inspected part, record the highest and lowest hardness values measured and compare to the requirement 39-42 HRC.
- Rationale: Through-hardness directly correlates with wear resistance and fatigue life in track link applications. Establishing a representative measurement practice ensures that variations from heat treatment or material chemistry are detected before assembly.

Bore diameter
- Purpose: Confirm bore concentricity and size meet functional fit for mating pins and rollers.
- Method: Measure bore diameter using a calibrated internal micrometer or plug gauge suitable for the nominal bore size. Measure along at least two orthogonal axes at the mid-length of the bore and at the bore entrances to detect taper. Record the measured values and calculate deviation from nominal. Acceptance criterion is ±0.02 mm as specified in the requirements table.
- Rationale: Bore tolerance ±0.02 mm is required to ensure

of acceptable and non-acceptable conditions
- Acceptable: Part with recorded hardness readings within the specified hardness range for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73), bore measurements all within the stated bore diameter tolerance ±0.10 mm, and recorded mass at or below the maximum forging weight 4.8 kg.
- Non-acceptable: Part with hardness readings outside 34-38 HRC; part with any bore measurement outside ±0.10 mm of nominal; forging with recorded mass greater than 4.8 kg.

Records to keep
- Heat/lot traceability record including incoming material certification and forging mass for each part.
- Hardness test records including instrument calibration identifier, test locations, and individual readings.
- Bore inspection records including measurement device identifier and raw measured values.
- Disposition records and nonconformance reports for any part that fails the stated requirements.
- Retain records per Plant P2 document retention policy and make available for internal audit and customer inquiries.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
- Any part found outside the limits stated in the requirements table shall be tagged as nonconforming and physically segregated from conforming inventory. Marking shall include the part identifier CFW-5998-73 and the reason for nonconformance.

Containment and notification
- Immediately notify production supervision and quality engineering. Capture the nonconformance on the official nonconformance report and attach the inspection records that triggered the report.

Evaluation and disposition
- Quality engineering and manufacturing engineering shall evaluate the cause and determine disposition. Possible dispositions include repair where feasible, rework under an approved procedure, scrap, or engineering review for use-as-is with customer approval. Any repair or rework proposal must include steps to ensure the repaired part will meet the requirements in the table and must be approved in writing by engineering.

Corrective action and records
- Root cause analysis shall be conducted for nonconformances that indicate a systemic issue. Implement corrective actions and document effectiveness. All disposition and corrective action records shall be filed with the lot records for the affected parts and made available for audits.

Revision control
- Changes to this specification require documented approval by quality engineering at Plant P2 and shall be recorded in the revision history.

diameter tolerance ±0.02 mm, or that exceeds the maximum forging weight 28.0 kg is nonconforming and must be segregated immediately from conforming material.

Disposition options
- Rework: Parts with conditionally correctable defects (for example, localized machining or rework that will restore bore size within ±0.02 mm) may be permitted to undergo controlled rework after written authorization from Quality. Rework must be documented and re-inspected to the same acceptance criteria, including verification of hardness within 39-42 HRC where heat or stress relief is applied.
- Repair by engineering: Where engineering assessment determines a repair that preserves function and safety is possible, Quality must approve a repair instruction and all repaired parts must be re-inspected to the original requirements.
- Scrap: Parts that cannot be returned to conformance, including those exceeding maximum forging weight 28.0 kg or those with through-hardness outside 39-42 HRC that cannot be corrected, shall be designated scrap and processed per site scrap control procedures.

Examples
- Example A: A forging measures a bore out-of-round such that one axis lies outside ±0.02 mm while the orthogonal axis is within ±0.02 mm. The part is segregated and evaluated for repair; if a permitted machining operation can restore the bore to within ±0.02 mm without altering hardness in relation to 39-42 HRC, rework may be authorized and the part reinspected.
- Example B: A forging weighs greater than maximum forging weight 28.0 kg. The part is nonconforming and shall be scrapped or returned to the forge for corrective action; it may not be reintroduced to production.

Audit and corrective action
- Quality shall track occurrences of nonconformance by characteristic and require root cause analysis for repeated failures against hardness 39-42 HRC, bore tolerance ±0.02 mm, or weight exceedance 28.0 kg. Corrective actions shall be proportionate to the failure mode and documented in corrective action records.

Revision and configuration
- This specification applies to part CFW-7661-91 as identified above. Changes to the requirements must be approved through the plant configuration control process.

Scope
This manual provides maintenance instructions and acceptance criteria for the Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) installed on line P3-L4. This quality specification defines the acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) manufactured from material grade 1045 at Plant P2. It applies to all finished forging deliveries and to in-process forgings proceeding to final machining at Plant P2. The intent is to control mechanical properties and critical dimensions that affect fit, performance, and service life.

Background and rationale: The connecting rod is a safety-critical rotating component. Hardness and bore control are primary determinants of wear life and fatigue performance after heat treatment and machining. Maximum forging weight governs lift and handling constraints for safe material flow and tooling limits. This document sets clear pass/fail criteria and inspection practices to ensure downstream machining and assembly stability.

## Requirements table

| Hardness (post-heat-treatment, finished) | The hardness range for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is 26-30 HRC. | Within specified range: Accept. Outside specified range: Reject. |

Requirements table shall be segregated and marked as nonconforming immediately. Do not release nonconforming parts for assembly or shipment.

Containment and evaluation
Perform containment to prevent further processing of affected material. Evaluate the extent of the nonconformance by determining if it is isolated to individual forgings or systemic across a production run. For hardness and bore tolerance failures, review the associated heat lot and die set run records to identify potential root causes. For parts exceeding the maximum forging weight of 28.4 kg, inspect the die trim and flash removal process and verify die maintenance records.

Disposition options and rationale
Acceptable dispositions include rework that demonstrably returns the part to conformance and is allowed by engineering drawing notes; controlled segregation for noncritical internal uses only if approved by engineering; or scrap. Rework that would alter the metallurgical condition (e.g., heat treatment) must be documented and validated by engineering prior to implementation. Parts that fail hardness criteria are generally not eligible for rework to meet mechanical property requirements without a documented and approved heat treatment plan. Parts exceeding the forging weight limit are often indicative of overfill and potential internal defects and must be evaluated for soundness before any rework decision.

Examples
Example of hardness failure response: a single forging reads outside 28-32 HRC at two locations. The lot is quarantined; three additional forgings from the same heat are sampled. If multiple parts are out of range, halt production, notify metallurgy, and coordinate a corrective action that may include hold, rework approval, or scrap. Record decisions and supporting test data.

Example of bore tolerance failure response: if an unmachined bore is outside ±0.10 mm, perform inspection of adjacent forgings in the run. If the issue is isolated, scrap or rework per engineering discretion; if systematic, review die fit, mandrel condition, and process parameters.

Records and corrective action
All nonconforming reports, investigation findings, root cause analyses, and corrective actions must be documented and retained with the lot quality file. Corrective actions should address immediate containment and long-term prevention, and shall include verification steps to confirm effectiveness.

Revision and control
This specification supersedes prior versions for Plant P3 production of connecting rod CFW-4516-94 (CFW-4516-94). Any deviations from this document require written engineering approval and must be recorded with justification and sign-off.

It covers metallurgical hardness, critical bore geometry, forging weight limits, visual and dimensional requirements where they affect fit or function, and the required records to demonstrate compliance.

Background and rationale
Connecting rod performance is controlled by core material properties and tight geometry at critical features. Hardness is used as a proxy for heat treatment and tensile properties; observed service and qualification testing require the rod to achieve a specific hardness band to ensure fatigue performance and bearing compatibility. Bore diameter tolerance is critical for journal fit and bearing clearance after machining; controlling bore tolerance at the forging stage minimizes downstream machining risk and ensures consistent wall thickness. Forging weight is controlled to manage die fill, internal soundness, and to limit defects associated with over- or under-filled impressions.

Requirements table

Scope

Scope
This document provides preventive maintenance, inspection, and corrective action guidance for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02). The intent is to ensure consistent billet heating performance, safe operation, and reliable integration with the ring rolling line. Tasks described apply to the heater housing, coil assembly, cooling system, power connections, controls, and instrumentation necessary to meet process targets and safety requirements. Reference procedures and quality requirements are identified at the end of the document; consult those documents for sampling, record retention, and permit requirements.

Background and rationale
EQ-P1-L2-IH02 is a medium-frequency induction billet heater used to heat forging billets prior to ring rolling. Maintaining coil integrity, cooling capacity, and accurate temperature control is critical to achieving metallurgical targets and preventing equipment damage. The target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 1230 °C. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 46 L/min. These values are process-critical: temperature directly affects microstructure and formability; cooling water flow prevents coil overheating and insulation failure. Maintenance tasks prioritize checks that ensure these two parameters can be reliably achieved and sustained.

- Personal protective equipment compliant with site requirements

- Lockout and tagout the heater power and energy sources per SOP-P1-L2-04 before opening panels or performing any work. Verify absence of hazardous energy and allow hot components to cool to safe touch levels.
- Review recent operating logs and alarm history for EQ-P1-L2-IH02 to identify recurring trends prior to disassembly.

External inspection
- Inspect external housing for deformation, signs of coolant leakage, or compromised cable entry seals

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4

Scope
This manual provides maintenance instructions and acceptance criteria for the Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) installed on line P3-L4. It covers preventive lubrication, clamp bolt torque verification, bearings inspection, and record keeping required to support safe, repeatable operation in the heat treat cell. This document aligns with shop best practices and references related procedural documents (SB-1028, SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-03).

Background and rationale
Radial ring rolling mills in heat treat service are subject to cyclic loading, elevated ambient conditions near furnaces, and contamination from scale and quench media. Critical interfaces include the mandrel clamp and main roll bearings. The mandrel clamp bolt preload directly affects ring control and concentricity during rolling; loss of preload can produce out-of-tolerance parts and pose safety risks. Main roll bearings require a consistent lubrication cadence to preserve film thickness and prevent premature fatigue. Prescribed torque and lubrication intervals are set to maintain preload and bearing life while accommodating the mill's operating environment.

- Calibrated torque wrench capable of applying the required clamp bolt torque as specified below, with current calibration certificate referenced in maintenance records.
- Clean, lint-free rags and approved bearing-grade grease compatible with the bearing manufacturer recommendations and SOP-P3-L4-02.
- Low-pressure grease gun compatible with the mill grease fittings.
- Inspection lamp and borescope for visual assessment of bearing seals and mandrel surfaces.
- Personal protective equipment as required by SOP-P3-L4-03 and SB-1028, including heat-resistant gloves and eye protection.
- Maintenance log forms and electronic entry device for records retention.

Critical values
- The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m.
- The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 160 hours.

Scope

This quality specification applies to the manufacture, inspection, and disposition of valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) machined from F316 forging stock at Plant P3. It defines critical quality requirements that must be met prior to release for assembly and shipment, and it establishes the accepted inspection methods, example acceptance criteria, and required records. Background information is provided to explain the rationale for each requirement and to aid inspection planning and nonconformance disposition.

Requirements table

| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) is 46.2 kg. |

The inspection method described here explains equipment selection, calibration requirements rationale, measurement approach, and sample-record examples to be retained.

Hardness verification
- Rationale: Hardness is a proxy for microstructure and heat treatment effectiveness in F316 forgings. The specified hardness controls machinability and wear characteristics while ensuring the material has not been over-tempered.
- Method: Verify hardness using a Rockwell hardness tester calibrated to the appropriate scale for HRC readings. Test locations must be representative of critical wall sections and machined surfaces. Document test locations and results on the inspection record.
- Acceptance: The hardness must meet the hardness range for valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) is 31-34 HRC. Any reading outside this range requires immediate hold of the affected lot and initiation of nonconformance handling.

Bore diameter verification

# QS-CFW-5042-83 Quality specification - valve body CFW-5042-83 (F316)

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3

Scope
This quality specification applies to the forged valve body CFW-5042-83 produced in Plant P3 from material grade F316. It establishes the mandatory acceptance requirements, the required inspection methods, and the process for managing nonconforming items. The purpose is to ensure forged parts meet functional and metallurgical criteria prior to machining and assembly, and that inspection records provide traceability for production and corrective action.

Requirements table
The following table lists the mandatory acceptance criteria for the valve body CFW-5042-83. These attributes are verified at final forge inspection and any subsequent operations that could affect the attribute.

| Attribute | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness range | 33-38 HRC | Hardness measured in the parent forged material, away from finish-machined surfaces. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.06 mm | Applies to the as-forged bore prior to final machining; control dimension for downstream fixtures. |
| Maximum forging weight | 77.3 kg | Net forging weight after flash removal and trimming, prior to heat treat and finish machining. |

Inspection method
General approach
Inspection shall be performed by qualified inspection personnel using calibrated instruments appropriate to each attribute. The inspection location is the final forge inspection area prior to heat treatment and machining. Records of inspections shall be retained with the heat lot and forging serial reference.

Hardness measurement
- Hardness testing shall be performed on representative forged surfaces in the parent metal, avoiding areas affected by trimming, heavy deformation, or tooling marks. Test locations shall be documented on the part record. Use a standardized hardness method suitable for HRC scale. Report measured values and note any readings outside the stated hardness range of 33-38 HRC. When borderline readings are encountered, additional tests on adjacent locations are documented until a clear condition is established. All hardness readings, test instrument identification, and calibration references are recorded on the inspection sheet.

Bore diameter verification
- The bore diameter tolerance of ±0.06 mm applies to the as-forged bore prior to machining. Bore inspection is performed with instruments capable of resolving to the tolerance band and set up to verify roundness and concentricity where applicable. Record the measured bore size, measurement method, and instrument identification.

Scope
This document defines the preventive maintenance procedure for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02). The intent is to preserve machine integrity, prevent unplanned downtime, and maintain product quality through recurring inspection and service activities focused on the mandrel clamp and main roll bearing system. This manual supplements and references standard operating procedures and engineering change notices listed in Related Documents. Tools

Use personal protective equipment consistent with plant standards and SOP-P3-L2-01.

Procedure
Background and rationale
Regular maintenance of the mandrel clamp and main roll bearings reduces risk of clamp slippage, mandrel runout, and bearing failure that can produce scrap rings or catastrophic equipment damage. The mandrel clamp bolt must be torqued to a validated value to maintain clamping force while avoiding fastener overstress. Main roll bearings require periodic lubrication to maintain an oil or grease film and to evacuate debris introduced during rolling.

Preparation
Follow SOP-P3-L2-01 for machine shutdown and electrical lockout. Verify that any changes in ECN-2026-044 have been implemented on the machine and that relevant schematics and fastener access points match the as-installed condition.

Mandrel clamp bolt torque

If the bolt shows evidence of damage, tag it out and initiate replacement per plant parts procedures; do not re-use damaged hardware.

Set the calibrated torque wrench to the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02), which is 475 N·m. Apply torque in a single continuous motion until the wrench indicates the set value. If a torque extension or adapter is used, compensate using a

## Scope
This document defines lubrication and fluid handling for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01). It covers lubricant selection, lubrication points, fluid storage and transfer precautions, and inspection acceptance criteria relevant to normal production and maintenance activities. This procedure applies to operations where the maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 995 mm. ## Background and rationale
Proper lubrication and fluid control on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 reduce wear, prevent seizure, and maintain dimensional stability of rolled rings. The specified lubricant minimizes metal-to-metal contact at sliding interfaces and is compatible with the machine's seals and bearings. Using the correct lubricant part number ensures supply chain traceability and material safety data sheet (MSDS) compliance: CFW-LUB-961.

This mill is used for rings up to the stated maximum outer diameter; larger rings require alternative equipment or process approval per ECN-2026-009. The goals of this document are to standardize lubrication practice, document inspection points, and define acceptance criteria for service records and fluid condition.

General approach
Inspections shall be performed by qualified personnel familiar with induction hardness testing, calibrated dimensional measurement instruments, and weighing equipment. Inspectors shall follow written procedures and record results on the indicated inspection form.

Hardness inspection
- Use a portable hardness tester suitable for Rockwell C measurements. Perform verification on calibrated reference blocks before use.
- Inspect hardness at a minimum of three locations representative of the forged web and flange area; avoid edge decarburized zones and through-hardened transitions. Document individual readings and compute the observed range for the part.
- Acceptance criterion: readings must fall within the hardness range specified above. If any reading falls outside the range, proceed to nonconformance handling.

Bore diameter inspection
- Measure bore diameter using calibrated bore gauges or inside micrometers appropriate for the bore size. Ensure measurement probes contact clean, cool surfaces free of scale.
- Take measurements at two axial positions and at orthogonal orientations to assess runout and local ovality; record each measurement and note the maximum deviation from nominal.
- Acceptance criterion: measured diameter must conform to the bore diameter tolerance specified above.

Weight verification
- Weigh the forging in its as-forged condition on a calibrated platform scale. Record the gross weight on the inspection record.
- Acceptance criterion: weight must not exceed the maximum forging weight specified above. If weight exceeds that value, follow nonconformance handling.

Examples and interpretation
- Example acceptable condition: hardness readings of values that lie within the specified hardness range across the sampled locations, bore measurements that stay within the specified bore tolerance, and weight under the maximum forging weight. Mark the part as acceptable and release to machining.

- Any part failing to meet one or more requirements shall be segregated and labeled with a nonconformance tag. Do not release for machining.

Scope
This document defines the preventive maintenance tasks, inspection criteria, and records required for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) in plant P3, line P3-L2. It covers routine access, lining inspection and replacement guidance, shot media replenishment, and verification activities needed to maintain cleaning performance and component life. Background and rationale
The shot blast cabinet is critical to surface preparation of ring-rolled forgings prior to downstream machining and inspection. Maintaining consistent media level preserves shot flow characteristics and reduces the risk of nozzle plugging and uneven blast coverage.

Scope

Activities include mechanical fastener verification, hydraulic system pressure verification, basic lubrication checks, and documentation practices required before returning the press to production.

Background and rationale

The main ram bolt secures the ram assembly and transmits forging loads to the frame. Fastener preload influences joint stiffness and fatigue life. The main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m. Adhering to this torque value ensures the fastener achieves the designed clamp load and joint performance.
- Hydraulic system overpressure is a primary hazard for seals, hoses, and valves. The system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 330 bar. Maintenance checks verify that safety devices and relief settings maintain system pressure within that limit.

- Hand tools for access panels, retaining hardware, and witness markings. Use non-sparking tools as required by local safety rules.

# MM-P3-L3-CN02 Maintenance manual - Machining CNC turning center #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-CN02

Scope
This document provides maintenance instructions for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02). It covers routine mechanical checks, chuck jaw bolt verification, spindle warm-up procedure prior to production, and required records. This manual is intended for qualified maintenance personnel and machine operators performing routine preventive maintenance and pre-production checks. Reference related procedural and safety requirements in MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1, SOP-P3-L3-02, and SOP-P3-L3-04.

Tools
Required items for the procedures that follow: calibrated torque wrench capable of applying the chuck jaw bolt torque specified below, basic hand tools, cleaning supplies appropriate for machine tool environments, lint-free shop cloths, manufacturer-approved lubricants and grease guns as called out in equipment manufacturer guidance, and the machine control pendant for executing spindle warm-up cycles. Ensure the torque wrench calibration certificate is available per traceability practice.

Procedure
Background and rationale
Proper clamping of workpieces and stable spindle operation are critical to part accuracy and operator safety. The chuck jaw bolts secure the jaws to the chuck body; incorrect bolt preload can lead to jaw loosening, runout, and component damage. The spindle assembly requires a controlled warm-up to achieve stable thermal conditions, which reduces dimensional drift during the initial production run.

Preparation
Verify machine is in a safe state for maintenance per SOP-P3-L3-02 and SOP-P3-L3-04. Lockout and tagout the machine as required by site practice before performing mechanical adjustments when exposed rotating elements are involved. Confirm presence of required tools and torque wrench calibration documentation. Consult MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1 for any model-specific notes.

Chuck jaw bolt torque verification
Inspect the chuck and jaws visually for debris, visible damage, or abnormal wear. Clean the mating surfaces of the jaw and chuck using an appropriate solvent and cloth. Seat the jaw on the chuck and hand-thread the jaw bolts to ensure proper engagement.

Set the calibrated torque wrench to the specified value and apply torque to each chuck jaw bolt in a cross-pattern sequence to achieve even preload. The chuck jaw bolt torque for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 75 N·m. After completing the torque sequence, perform a second pass to verify bolts remain at

[doc:MM-P3-L3-CN02] Maintenance manual - Machining CNC turning center #2
specified value and apply torque to each chuck jaw bolt in a cross-pattern sequence to achieve even preload. The chuck jaw bolt torque for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 75 N·m. After completing the torque sequence, perform a second pass to verify bolts remain at the specified torque.

Rationale: Applying the specified torque ensures consistent clamping force and prevents loosening during operation. Using a cross pattern equalizes load and minimizes distortion of the chuck face.

Spindle warm-up
Prior to loading hardened work material or beginning critical production, perform the spindle warm-up routine with the machine in run-permit state. Activate the spindle warm-up cycle using the control pendant and monitor spindle behavior throughout the sequence. The spindle warm-up time for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 24 minutes.

Rationale: Gradual thermal stabilization of spindle bearings and spindle headstock reduces dimensional drift and runout, improving first-piece accuracy and prolonging bearing life.

If a jaw bolt fails to reach the specified torque without evidence of thread strip or damage, remove the bolt and inspect threads and mating insert. Record observations and any corrective actions taken.

The log entry should include the equipment id, date, personnel performing the action, confirmation that the chuck jaw bolt torque was set to 75 N·m, confirmation that the spindle warm-up was completed for 24 minutes, and any anomalies or corrective actions. Scope
This document defines quality acceptance criteria and inspection methods for the crankshaft blank identified as CFW-9184-50, manufactured from steel grade 4340, produced at Plant P3. The intent is to establish mandatory material and dimensional acceptance criteria, outline the inspection methodology to demonstrate conformity, and provide a consistent process for handling nonconforming items. This specification applies to raw forged blanks prior to finish machining and heat treatment operations.

Background and rationale
Crankshaft blanks for high-cycle rotating assemblies require controlled hardness and accurate bore location to ensure final machining yield and finished-component performance. The values stated in this document reflect metallurgical and machining constraints established by design engineering. Inspectors and quality engineers must verify the stated requirements on incoming and in-process forgings to avoid downstream scrap, rework, and latent field failures. The inspection methods described favor traceable, instrumented measurements and documented records to support first article verification and routine production checks.

Requirements table
| Attribute | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Material | 4340 (as specified on part drawing) |
| Hardness range | The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is 32-38 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is ±0.02 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is 80.8 kg. |
| Surface condition | Free of forging laps, cold shuts, and separation defects that would affect machinability or structural integrity (visual and tactile inspection). |
| Traceability | Each forging must be legibly stamped or tagged with the part identifier and a batch or heat number that links to mill certificates. |

Inspection method
General approach
Inspections are performed using calibrated instruments and documented procedures. The emphasis is on objective data capture, clear acceptance criteria, and retention of records that enable traceability to the production batch.

For full preventive maintenance schedules and detailed component replacement procedures, see MM-P1-L1-IH03. Operational startup and shutdown procedures are covered in SOP-P1-L1-03 and SOP-P1-L1-05.

Background and rationale
Calibration checks on induction billet heaters ensure consistent heating performance, safe operation, and predictable billet quality. The coil assembly, sensing elements, and control feedback loops are susceptible to drift and mechanical wear from thermal cycling and vibration. Regular verification detects changes before they affect forging quality or cause unplanned downtime. To reduce risk, this document emphasizes verifying sensor linearity, coil condition, and control loop response. The coil inspection interval for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 290 hours. Adhering to this interval aligns coil condition monitoring with heating duty cycles and minimizes the chance of insulation failure or shorting.

Tools
- Appropriate multimeter and insulation resistance tester rated for the equipment voltage class.
- Portable oscilloscope or control-loop analyzer for verifying waveform shape and timing.
- Contact thermometer or non-contact temperature verification device for spot checks of sensor outputs against expected values.
- Hand tools and insulated handling tools as required by site safety policy.
- Approved lubricant for moving linkages and bearings: CFW-LUB-188.
- Personal protective equipment as required by plant standards.

Procedure
Pre-checks and safety

- Inspect cooling hose and fittings for chafing, hardening, or contamination. Clean and secure fittings as needed. Rationale: mechanical wear can cause leaks that reduce flow and allow air ingress that degrades cooling effectiveness.

Cooling system verification

Verify that the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is achieved. Rationale: flow at or above the specified minimum is required to remove heat from the coil and prevent thermal runaway.
- Record flow meter readings and note any transient variability. If flow is below the required minimum, execute corrective actions per SB-1009 and stop heating operations until resolved.

Electrical and control checks
- With power re-applied under controlled conditions per SOP-P1-L1-01, perform insulation resistance checks to the grounded structure using approved test equipment. Observe manufacturer guidance for acceptable procedures as referenced in MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3.
- Verify control interlocks and safety trips related to coil temperature and cooling flow are operational. Rationale: interlocks are the last line of defense against equipment damage.

## Scope
This quality specification establishes acceptance criteria, inspection practices, and nonconformance handling for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) produced at Plant P3. It applies to all forged, heat treated, and machined track links delivered under part number CFW-1159-60 for customer orders and internal inventory. The document defines required measurements, allowable tolerances, inspection methods, documentation to be retained, and disposition instructions for nonconforming material.

Background and intent: track links are safety-critical wear components. The controls in this specification are intended to ensure dimensional accuracy, material condition, and hardness consistent with design requirements and downstream assembly fitment. Where measurement choices require judgment, the inspection method section provides examples and rationale to support consistent application by quality and production personnel.

## Requirements

| Item | Requirement | Acceptance |
|------|-------------|------------|
| Hardness | The hardness range for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is 36-40 HRC. | Must be within stated range across inspected locations. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is ±0.03 mm. | Measured bore diameter must be within nominal plus or minus stated tolerance. |
| Forging weight | The maximum forging weight for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is 80.0 kg. | Raw forging weight must not exceed stated maximum. |

Notes on table application: Acceptance applies to sampled or 100 percent inspected parts as specified in the production routing and as required by the purchase order. References to "nominal" in the bore entry refer to the drawing nominal diameter called out on the engineering drawing for CFW-1159-60.

## Inspection method

General approach: Inspection shall verify each requirement in the table using calibrated instruments and documented procedures. Inspectors shall be trained on the equipment and methods used and shall follow practices that minimize measurement variation.

Hardness measurement
- Hardness shall be verified using a Rockwell hardness tester calibrated to the HRC scale and operated per the instrument manufacturer's procedure. Impact of surface

Inspection method
- Visual inspection: Inspect each part for forging defects that could affect fit or function, such as laps, cold shuts, cracks, and significant surface inclusions. Use magnification as required to confirm suspected discontinuities. Parts with suspected internal discontinuities shall be segregated pending further nondestructive evaluation.
- Dimensional inspection: Verify bore diameter at specified locations using calibrated bore gauges or coordinate measuring equipment capable of reading to the specified drawing resolution. Compare measurements directly to the nominal drawing dimension and the bore diameter tolerance of ±0.03 mm. Record measured values on the inspection record.
- Hardness testing: Perform hardness testing on the through-hardened area using a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester set to the appropriate scale. Take measurements at the specified locations detailed on the inspection drawing. The hardness range for track link CFW-5753-95 (CFW-5753-95) is 34-37 HRC; parts must exhibit values within this range. If hardness readings vary across locations, record all readings and hold the lot until disposition is determined.
- Weight verification: Weigh each forging on a calibrated scale to confirm the forging weight does not exceed the maximum forging weight 28.3 kg. For batches where full-piece weighing is not practical, perform representative checks and escalate to 100 percent weighing if any sample exceeds the maximum.
- Nondestructive testing: Where indicated by process control or suspect indications from visual inspection, perform magnetic particle inspection or ultrasonic testing per the applicable procedure. Record results and attach to the inspection log.

Rationale and examples
- Hardness rationale: Maintaining hardness within 34-37 HRC ensures a balance between wear resistance and fracture toughness. For example, a part hardened above the specified range may be brittle under impact; a part below may wear prematurely in service.
- Bore tolerance rationale: The bore tolerance of ±0.03 mm controls fit with mating pins and affects assembly preload and track articulation. An out-of-tolerance bore can produce premature wear or assembly interference.
- Weight rationale: The maximum forging weight 28.3 kg guards against excessive material that can indicate incorrect die fill, excessive flash, or material defects. For example, an over-weight forging may not properly heat treat or may contain hidden inclusions that compromise integrity.

Nonconformance handling
- Segregation: Immediately segregate any part or lot that fails to meet any requirement in the table. Mark segregation tags with the part number, lot identifier,

Disposition options
- Rework: Parts with conditionally correctable defects (for example, localized machining or rework that will restore bore size within ±0.02 mm) may be permitted to undergo controlled rework after written authorization from Quality. Rework must be documented and re-inspected to the same acceptance criteria, including verification of hardness within 39-42 HRC where heat or stress relief is applied.
- Repair by engineering: Where engineering assessment determines a repair that preserves function and safety is possible, Quality must approve a repair instruction and all repaired parts must be re-inspected to the original requirements.
- Scrap: Parts that cannot be returned to conformance, including those exceeding maximum forging weight 28.0 kg or those with through-hardness outside 39-42 HRC that cannot be corrected, shall be designated scrap and processed per site scrap control procedures.

Examples
- Example A: A forging measures a bore out-of-round such that one axis lies outside ±0.02 mm while the orthogonal axis is within ±0.02 mm. The part is segregated and evaluated for repair; if a permitted machining operation can restore the bore to within ±0.02 mm without altering hardness in relation to 39-42 HRC, rework may be authorized and the part reinspected.
- Example B: A forging weighs greater than maximum forging weight 28.0 kg. The part is nonconforming and shall be scrapped or returned to the forge for corrective action; it may not be reintroduced to production.

Audit and corrective action
- Quality shall track occurrences of nonconformance by characteristic and require root cause analysis for repeated failures against hardness 39-42 HRC, bore tolerance ±0.02 mm, or weight exceedance 28.0 kg. Corrective actions shall be proportionate to the failure mode and documented in corrective action records.

Acceptable dispositions include rework that demonstrably returns the part to conformance and is allowed by engineering drawing notes; controlled segregation for noncritical internal uses only if approved by engineering; or scrap. Rework that would alter the metallurgical condition (e.g., heat treatment) must be documented and validated by engineering prior to implementation. Parts that fail hardness criteria are generally not eligible for rework to meet mechanical property requirements without a documented and approved heat treatment plan. Parts exceeding the forging weight limit are often indicative of overfill and potential internal defects and must be evaluated for soundness before any rework decision.

Examples
Example of hardness failure response: a single forging reads outside 28-32 HRC at two locations. The lot is quarantined; three additional forgings from the same heat are sampled. If multiple parts are out of range, halt production, notify metallurgy, and coordinate a corrective action that may include hold, rework approval, or scrap. Record decisions and supporting test data.

Example of bore tolerance failure response: if an unmachined bore is outside ±0.10 mm, perform inspection of adjacent forgings in the run. If the issue is isolated, scrap or rework per engineering discretion; if systematic, review die fit, mandrel condition, and process parameters.

Records and corrective action
All nonconforming reports, investigation findings, root cause analyses, and corrective actions must be documented and retained with the lot quality file. Corrective actions should address immediate containment and long-term prevention, and shall include verification steps to confirm effectiveness.

Revision and control
This specification supersedes prior versions for Plant P3 production of connecting rod CFW-4516-94 (CFW-4516-94). Any deviations from this document require written engineering approval and must be recorded with justification and sign-off.

Scope
This manual defines required maintenance activities, rationale, and records for Ring Rolling induction billet heater EQ-P2-L2-IH01. It covers routine inspection, preventive maintenance, and corrective actions needed to maintain safe and reliable operation. This document is intended for maintenance technicians and engineers responsible for furnace performance and material quality. Refer to ECN-2026-012, ECN-2026-048, and SOP-P2-L2-05 for related design changes, electrical schematics, and plant operating procedures.

Background and performance target
The induction billet heater is used to bring feedstock to forming temperature prior to ring rolling. The target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 1230 °C. Maintaining uniform temperature profile and consistent coil cooling prevents premature coil degradation and ensures repeatable ring geometry. Coil cooling water must meet flow requirements to avoid coil overheating; the coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 81 L/min.

Tools and consumables
- Insulation-safe temperature probe compatible with high-temperature billet measurement as called out in SOP-P2-L2-05.  
- Infrared thermometer for surface checks and verification.  
- Multimeter and clamp ammeter for electrical checks per ECN-2026-048.  
- Spanner set, insulated hand tools, lifting strap suitable for coil handling.  
- Replacement coil fasteners and insulation panels specified in ECN-2026-012.  
- Degreasing solvent and lint-free cloths for coil and connector cleaning.  
- Maintenance log forms and electronic entry device per plant document control.

Procedure
Preparation and safety
- Review SOP-P2-L2-05 and coordinate with line control before entry. Lockout and tagout all power supplies to EQ-P2-L2-IH01 and post signage at the line staging area. Verify absence of residual charge using appropriate procedures in ECN-2026-048 prior to touching exposed conductors. Wear heat-rated gloves and eye protection when working near recent heat cycles.

Visual inspection
- Inspect induction coil assembly for visible deformation, cracking, or discoloration indicative of overheating.

[doc:FAQ-004] Engineering FAQ #4
The spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes. ## Scope
This quality specification defines acceptance criteria and inspection methods for the manufactured track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60) produced at Plant P1. It applies to forged parts delivered to assembly, parts returned from heat treatment, and finished parts submitted for final inspection. The document covers material condition, dimensional control of the bore, hardness acceptance, inspection procedures, sampling rationale, and controls for nonconforming items. This specification is intended for use by production, quality, and metallurgical personnel.

## Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|

Rationale: The hardness band is selected to ensure adequate wear resistance while maintaining toughness for the dynamic loading environment of the track link. The bore tolerance is dictated by mating component fit and lubrication retention requirements. The maximum forging weight reflects handling and die capacity constraints at Plant P1.

## Inspection method
General approach
- Inspectors shall verify each characteristic in the Requirements table prior to release to the next operation. Records must document the inspector identity, inspection equipment used, and results observed.
- Calibration status of all measuring equipment shall be verified against the calibration control system prior to use. Use equipment with appropriate resolution and repeatability for the characteristic measured.

Hardness verification
- Hardness shall be measured on a minimum of one location representative of the bore region on every finished part. If part geometry prevents direct indentation in the bore, an adjacent location that has undergone identical heat treatment and machining shall be used. When a part is measured, record the instrument identifier and reading. Acceptance is granted only when the measured value falls within 31-35 HRC.
- If a measured value is outside the specified range, follow the nonconformance handling section below.

Bore diameter measurement
- Measure the bore diameter after final machining using a bore gauge or
