a bore outside ±0.03 mm, or a hardness reading outside 31-35 HRC, is subject to the nonconformance process and may require rework, segregation, or scrap.

## Nonconformance handling
Segregation and hold
- Any item that fails to meet the Requirements table shall be immediately segregated and labeled as nonconforming. Do not release nonconforming items to downstream operations without documented disposition.

Disposition options
- Rework: If the deviation is something that can be corrected by defined machining or heat treatment processes without compromising part integrity, a controlled rework plan may be approved by quality engineering. Reworked parts must be re-inspected to demonstrate compliance with the Requirements table.
- Use-as-is: Rare dispositions for use-as-is must be supported by engineering analysis demonstrating that functional performance is not compromised and must be approved by authorized engineering personnel. The basis for approval must be documented and retained.
- Scrap: Parts that cannot be reworked or approved for use-as-is shall be scrapped and recorded.

Investigation and corrective action
- For any recurring nonconformance, initiate a root cause investigation. Document findings, corrective actions, and verification steps. Implement corrective action to prevent recurrence and verify effectiveness through subsequent inspection results.

Notifications and records
- Notify production supervision and quality management of any nonconformance that affects delivery or safety. Maintain records of nonconformance forms, dispositions, investigation reports, and corrective action records in the document control and quality management systems.

Audit and review
- Quality shall periodically review inspection records to confirm continued conformance to this specification and to identify any trends. Findings and corrective actions shall be recorded and retained as part of the plant quality records.

End of specification.

Requirements table shall be segregated and marked as nonconforming immediately. Do not release nonconforming parts for assembly or shipment.

Containment and evaluation
Perform containment to prevent further processing of affected material. Evaluate the extent of the nonconformance by determining if it is isolated to individual forgings or systemic across a production run. For hardness and bore tolerance failures, review the associated heat lot and die set run records to identify potential root causes. For parts exceeding the maximum forging weight of 28.4 kg, inspect the die trim and flash removal process and verify die maintenance records.

Disposition options and rationale
Acceptable dispositions include rework that demonstrably returns the part to conformance and is allowed by engineering drawing notes; controlled segregation for noncritical internal uses only if approved by engineering; or scrap. Rework that would alter the metallurgical condition (e.g., heat treatment) must be documented and validated by engineering prior to implementation. Parts that fail hardness criteria are generally not eligible for rework to meet mechanical property requirements without a documented and approved heat treatment plan. Parts exceeding the forging weight limit are often indicative of overfill and potential internal defects and must be evaluated for soundness before any rework decision.

Examples
Example of hardness failure response: a single forging reads outside 28-32 HRC at two locations. The lot is quarantined; three additional forgings from the same heat are sampled. If multiple parts are out of range, halt production, notify metallurgy, and coordinate a corrective action that may include hold, rework approval, or scrap. Record decisions and supporting test data.

Example of bore tolerance failure response: if an unmachined bore is outside ±0.10 mm, perform inspection of adjacent forgings in the run. If the issue is isolated, scrap or rework per engineering discretion; if systematic, review die fit, mandrel condition, and process parameters.

Records and corrective action
All nonconforming reports, investigation findings, root cause analyses, and corrective actions must be documented and retained with the lot quality file. Corrective actions should address immediate containment and long-term prevention, and shall include verification steps to confirm effectiveness.

Scope
This quality specification defines the acceptance criteria and inspection methods for the track link CFW-7661-91 (CFW-7661-91). It applies to forgings delivered to P1 and to all in-plant operations that affect final hardness, bore diameter, and forging weight. The intent is to ensure functional interchangeability and service life consistent with design requirements for the CFW-7661-91 family.

Requirements table
The table below lists the mandatory quality attributes and acceptance criteria for CFW-7661-91.

| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Through-hardness | 39-42 HRC | All finished inspection points must fall within 39-42 HRC |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.02 mm | Measured bores must be within nominal dimension ±0.02 mm |
| Forging weight | Maximum forging weight 28.0 kg | Any forging exceeding 28.0 kg is rejected for this part number |

Inspection method
Hardness
- Purpose: Verify through-hardness distribution meets the requirement 39-42 HRC for CFW-7661-91.
- Method: Use a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester and apply the manufacturer’s standard procedure for HRC measurement on steel forgings. Measurements shall be taken at locations representative of service-critical sections including the girth area and the bore collar. For each inspected part, record the highest and lowest hardness values measured and compare to the requirement 39-42 HRC.
- Rationale: Through-hardness directly correlates with wear resistance and fatigue life in track link applications. Establishing a representative measurement practice ensures that variations from heat treatment or material chemistry are detected before assembly.

Bore diameter
- Purpose: Confirm bore concentricity and size meet functional fit for mating pins and rollers.
- Method: Measure bore diameter using a calibrated internal micrometer or plug gauge suitable for the nominal bore size. Measure along at least two orthogonal axes at the mid-length of the bore and at the bore entrances to detect taper. Record the measured values and calculate deviation from nominal. Acceptance criterion is ±0.02 mm as specified in the requirements table.
- Rationale: Bore tolerance ±0.02 mm is required to ensure

diameter tolerance ±0.02 mm, or that exceeds the maximum forging weight 28.0 kg is nonconforming and must be segregated immediately from conforming material.

Disposition options
- Rework: Parts with conditionally correctable defects (for example, localized machining or rework that will restore bore size within ±0.02 mm) may be permitted to undergo controlled rework after written authorization from Quality. Rework must be documented and re-inspected to the same acceptance criteria, including verification of hardness within 39-42 HRC where heat or stress relief is applied.
- Repair by engineering: Where engineering assessment determines a repair that preserves function and safety is possible, Quality must approve a repair instruction and all repaired parts must be re-inspected to the original requirements.
- Scrap: Parts that cannot be returned to conformance, including those exceeding maximum forging weight 28.0 kg or those with through-hardness outside 39-42 HRC that cannot be corrected, shall be designated scrap and processed per site scrap control procedures.

Examples
- Example A: A forging measures a bore out-of-round such that one axis lies outside ±0.02 mm while the orthogonal axis is within ±0.02 mm. The part is segregated and evaluated for repair; if a permitted machining operation can restore the bore to within ±0.02 mm without altering hardness in relation to 39-42 HRC, rework may be authorized and the part reinspected.
- Example B: A forging weighs greater than maximum forging weight 28.0 kg. The part is nonconforming and shall be scrapped or returned to the forge for corrective action; it may not be reintroduced to production.

Audit and corrective action
- Quality shall track occurrences of nonconformance by characteristic and require root cause analysis for repeated failures against hardness 39-42 HRC, bore tolerance ±0.02 mm, or weight exceedance 28.0 kg. Corrective actions shall be proportionate to the failure mode and documented in corrective action records.

Revision and configuration
- This specification applies to part CFW-7661-91 as identified above. Changes to the requirements must be approved through the plant configuration control process.

Requirements table shall be segregated and marked as nonconforming immediately. Do not release nonconforming parts for assembly or shipment.

Containment and evaluation
Perform containment to prevent further processing of affected material. Evaluate the extent of the nonconformance by determining if it is isolated to individual forgings or systemic across a production run. For hardness and bore tolerance failures, review the associated heat lot and die set run records to identify potential root causes. For parts exceeding the maximum forging weight of 28.4 kg, inspect the die trim and flash removal process and verify die maintenance records.

Disposition options and rationale
Acceptable dispositions include rework that demonstrably returns the part to conformance and is allowed by engineering drawing notes; controlled segregation for noncritical internal uses only if approved by engineering; or scrap. Rework that would alter the metallurgical condition (e.g., heat treatment) must be documented and validated by engineering prior to implementation. Parts that fail hardness criteria are generally not eligible for rework to meet mechanical property requirements without a documented and approved heat treatment plan. Parts exceeding the forging weight limit are often indicative of overfill and potential internal defects and must be evaluated for soundness before any rework decision.

Examples
Example of hardness failure response: a single forging reads outside 28-32 HRC at two locations. The lot is quarantined; three additional forgings from the same heat are sampled. If multiple parts are out of range, halt production, notify metallurgy, and coordinate a corrective action that may include hold, rework approval, or scrap. Record decisions and supporting test data.

Example of bore tolerance failure response: if an unmachined bore is outside ±0.10 mm, perform inspection of adjacent forgings in the run. If the issue is isolated, scrap or rework per engineering discretion; if systematic, review die fit, mandrel condition, and process parameters.

Records and corrective action
All nonconforming reports, investigation findings, root cause analyses, and corrective actions must be documented and retained with the lot quality file. Corrective actions should address immediate containment and long-term prevention, and shall include verification steps to confirm effectiveness.

Revision and control

Perform containment to prevent further processing of affected material. Evaluate the extent of the nonconformance by determining if it is isolated to individual forgings or systemic across a production run. For hardness and bore tolerance failures, review the associated heat lot and die set run records to identify potential root causes. Disposition options and rationale
Acceptable dispositions include rework that demonstrably returns the part to conformance and is allowed by engineering drawing notes; controlled segregation for noncritical internal uses only if approved by engineering; or scrap. Rework that would alter the metallurgical condition (e.g., heat treatment) must be documented and validated by engineering prior to implementation. Parts that fail hardness criteria are generally not eligible for rework to meet mechanical property requirements without a documented and approved heat treatment plan. Parts exceeding the forging weight limit are often indicative of overfill and potential internal defects and must be evaluated for soundness before any rework decision.

Examples
Example of hardness failure response: a single forging reads outside 28-32 HRC at two locations. The lot is quarantined; three additional forgings from the same heat are sampled. If multiple parts are out of range, halt production, notify metallurgy, and coordinate a corrective action that may include hold, rework approval, or scrap. Record decisions and supporting test data.

Example of bore tolerance failure response: if an unmachined bore is outside ±0.10 mm, perform inspection of adjacent forgings in the run. If the issue is isolated, scrap or rework per engineering discretion; if systematic, review die fit, mandrel condition, and process parameters.

Records and corrective action
All nonconforming reports, investigation findings, root cause analyses, and corrective actions must be documented and retained with the lot quality file. Corrective actions should address immediate containment and long-term prevention, and shall include verification steps to confirm effectiveness.

This specification supersedes prior versions for Plant P3 production of connecting rod CFW-4516-94 (CFW-4516-94). Any deviations from this document require written engineering approval and must be recorded with justification and sign-off.

# MM-P1-L4-HT03 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3

Scope
This document defines the preventative maintenance, calibration, and verification tasks required to maintain the Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3, identified as EQ-P1-L4-HT03, in a condition that ensures process control and product conformance. The scope covers austenitizing controls, thermocouple calibration, control loop checks, door seals, atmosphere control verification, and recordkeeping required by plant quality and safety programs. Related documents include ECN-2026-002, SB-1006, and SOP-P1-L4-02 and must be consulted for change notices, safety bulletins, and operating procedures.

Background and rationale
The furnace is used for critical heat treat cycles where core microstructure and mechanical properties are sensitive to temperature uniformity and setpoint accuracy. The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C. Maintaining accurate temperature measurement and control at this setpoint is essential to avoid under- or over-austenitizing, which can lead to nonconforming forgings. Thermocouple drift and control loop degradation are the most common sources of process deviation; therefore, a dedicated calibration and verification regimen is required. The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 95 days.

Tools and materials
- Calibrated reference temperature source appropriate for high-temperature thermocouple checks (refer to SB-1006 for equipment approval).  
- Portable thermocouple calibrator and cold-junction reference.  
- Replacement thermocouple elements and connectors approved for use in EQ-P1-L4-HT03.  
- Door seal inspection kit and approved gasketing materials.  
- Logbooks, electronic maintenance entry device, or CMMS entry template per SOP-P1-L4-02.  
- Personal protective equipment as required by ECN-2026-002 and plant safety rules.

Procedure
Prepare

Scope
This manual prescribes preventive maintenance, inspection, calibration, and acceptance criteria for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02). It applies to maintenance technicians and furnace operators responsible for safe operation, metallurgical control, and traceable records retention. Activities described here are intended to maintain process capability, safety interlocks, and repeatable thermal profiles required by process engineering and quality assurance.

Background and rationale
Maintaining stable austenitizing and cooling profiles in EQ-P3-L4-HT02 is essential to achieve specified microstructure and mechanical properties in forged components. Out-of-tolerance temperatures or degraded thermocouple performance lead to nonconforming parts and potential rework. This manual aligns with change control and operating procedures; see ECN-2026-001 for design changes and SOP-P3-L4-02 and SOP-P3-L4-05 for operation and control-zone responsibilities. Calibration of temperature sensing and verification of setpoints ensure process reproducibility and regulatory traceability.

Critical settings
The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 885 °C.  
The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 110 days.

Tools and consumables
- Portable data logger capable of NIST-traceable calibration and independent of furnace controller.  
- Spare temperature-sensing elements compatible with furnace input, logged and tagged as calibrated.  
- Non-sparking hand tools for enclosure service, insulated handling gloves, and PPE per site rules.  
- Pre-approved calibration bath or dry-block standard against which thermocouples are compared.  
- Maintenance log forms and electronic records access to document results and corrective actions.

Procedure

- Verify lockout-tagout and safety clearance per SOP-P3-L4-05 before any maintenance or calibration work begins.  
- Ensure records from the previous inspection are available for review and that ECN-2026-001 changes are incorporated into wiring and controller settings where applicable.

Revision: Rev D

Reason for change
- Background: Recent maintenance audits and lubricant analysis samples identified accelerated wear signatures on the main roll bearings of the Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01). Trending in vibration and oil particle counts, reviewed against the existing maintenance practice, indicates that lubrication frequency is a principal contributor to the observed condition. Laboratory commentary recommended shortening the time between replenishment to reduce contamination loading and restore hydrodynamic film integrity.
- Objective: Standardize the main roll bearing lubrication to a defined interval to reduce wear rates, extend component life, and reduce unplanned downtime risk. This change aligns maintenance practice with the findings in related engineering notices and standard operating procedures to ensure consistent application across the line and supporting documentation.
- Rationale: Implementing a documented, shorter lubrication interval provides a simple, auditable action that directly addresses the root-cause indicators from oil analysis and bearing inspections. The interval decision was selected to balance operational availability with lubricant contamination control, minimize bearing metal-to-metal contact risk, and provide a repeatable baseline for future trend analysis and corrective actions.

Affected items
- Equipment affected: Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01).  
- Components affected: Main roll bearings and associated lubrication system components (feed lines, reservoirs, strainers, and gauge points used for sampling).  
- Documentation affected: Maintenance task lists and log templates for EQ-P1-L1-RR01; operator shift handover checklists that include bearing condition notes; lubrication consumption and inventory records; oil analysis sampling schedule records used for trend tracking. See related documents ECN-2026-034 and ECN-2026-040 for prior condition assessments and supporting analysis, and SOP-P1-L1-02 for operating interface and handover requirements.

Implementation
- New requirement: The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 120 hours. This interval supersedes prior informal practice and becomes the controlled interval to be recorded in maintenance execution and equipment history records.

# MM-P1-L1-RR01 Maintenance manual - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01

Scope
-------
This document establishes required preventive maintenance and controlled adjustment procedures for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1, EQ-P1-L1-RR01. It covers the mandrel clamp bolt torque setting and main roll bearing lubrication interval, inspection rationale, safe handling notes, example record entries, and criteria for acceptance after maintenance activities. Refer to SB-1025 for safety barriers and to SOP-P1-L1-01 and SOP-P1-L1-05 for lockout, permit, and standard operating procedures that apply during execution.

Background and rationale
------------------------
Radial ring rolling mills subject the mandrel and bearing systems to high mechanical loads and thermal cycles. Proper clamp bolt preload and disciplined lubrication intervals maintain alignment, minimize fretting, and extend component life. The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 635 N·m. The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 120 hours. These values are field-proven for the installed assemblies and must not be modified without engineering authorization and cross reference to supplier documentation.

Tools
-----
Required items for the procedures below are general maintenance hand tools, calibration equipment, and records. Use industry standard torque wrench and calibrated oil cup or grease dispensing system per SOP-P1-L1-05. Personal protective equipment should follow SB-1025 and SOP-P1-L1-01. Keep a calibrated torque wrench with current calibration certificate available. Maintain a lubrication log and a clamp torque verification record in the equipment file.

Scope
This manual describes the preventive and corrective maintenance required to maintain safe, repeatable heat treat cycles for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03). The content focuses on the furnace systems that affect metallurgical outcomes: atmosphere control, heating elements, thermocouple integrity, door seals, and the control system. For shipping and spares bulletins, reference SB-1015 and SB-1041.

Tools and consumables
Required tools are those commonly used for furnace maintenance and instrumentation work, including calibrated handheld thermometry, insulation handling tools, soft nonmetallic scrapers, and instrumentation hand tools appropriate for the control vendor. Consumables include replacement thermocouples matched to the control system, replacement door seals compatible with the furnace design, high temperature gasket cement manufacturer recommended for this furnace, and cleaning solvents approved in plant procedures. Ensure all tools and consumables are approved by maintenance supervision and are traceable in stores.

Maintaining the austenitizing setpoint and thermocouple accuracy directly affects microstructure, mechanical properties, and scrap rates for ring rolling feedstock. The specified austenitizing setpoint ensures full austenitization of the chosen steel grades while minimizing excessive grain growth. Thermocouple drift over time can produce significant process variation; the stated calibration interval is set to balance downtime and process control risk. The maintenance actions in this manual are designed to detect and correct common failure modes that lead to setpoint deviation or thermal nonuniformity.

Preliminary steps
Confirm control system alarms are acknowledged and logged prior to work. Isolate power and follow the lockout procedure in SOP-P3-L2-01. Verify the furnace chamber is at ambient conditions before removing insulation or accessing internal components.

Inspection of heating elements and insulation
Visually inspect heating elements for breaks, deformation, or discoloration indicative of overheating. Inspect insulation modules for compression, bridging, or contamination from scale or quench residue. Remove loose debris with nonmetallic tools and vacuum with approved high temperature vacuum equipment. Replace insulation modules showing loss of shape or breaches in the compressive face. When reinstalling insulation, seat modules to prevent hot spots at element supports.

Door seal and mechanical system
Inspect the door seal for continuity, tears, or separation from the backing. Clean mating surfaces and apply approved gasket cement where minor gaps are present. If the seal shows material breakdown or there is evidence of gas leakage during a heat cycle, install the replacement seal per vendor guidance. Verify door hinge and latch function and that door closes uniformly. Adjustments should be made to ensure an even contact surface between the door seal and furnace face.

Thermocouple inspection and calibration
Inspect thermocouple leads and junctions for mechanical damage, abrasions, or loose fittings at process connections. Replace any thermocouple showing physical damage. The thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 55 days; schedule calibration events in maintenance planning to ensure continuity of control accuracy. During calibration, perform a comparison against a laboratory reference standard following the control vendor procedure and record the correction factors. If a thermocouple shows deviation beyond the vendor tolerance, replace it and document the replacement.

Control system and atmosphere control
Verify control loops for heating zones are responding and that setpoint tracking is within expected behavior. Confirm atmosphere supply and return lines are free of obstructions and that purge cycles operate per process requirements. Inspect atmosphere generator components and filtration per SB-1015 guidance for spares and replacement items. Log any variances and tag components for corrective action.

Corrective repairs
For element failure, replace elements using the manufacturer specified replacement items. For insulation breaches, replace affected modules. For control card failures, refer to SB-1041 for spare card handling and vendor contact information. After any corrective repair, perform a controlled heat cycle using an empty load to validate uniformity and control accuracy before returning the furnace to production.

Scope
This document defines preventive maintenance and verification tasks for the Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) used in the P2 line. It covers the austenitizing setpoint verification, thermocouple calibration schedule, general furnace checks, and the acceptance criteria required to return the furnace to production. This manual is intended for maintenance technicians and heat treat operators and supplements operating procedures SOP-P2-L2-02 and SOP-P2-L2-05. See also MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1 for parts and spares information.

Background and rationale
The stability of the austenitizing temperature directly affects microstructure and dimensional repeatability of ring-rolled components. Thermocouple accuracy and sensor placement are critical to achieving consistent metallurgical results. The procedures in this manual are structured to verify that the furnace reaches and holds the specified austenitizing setpoint and that thermocouples are within calibration tolerance before production cycles. Where calibration or repairs are required, documented evidence is retained to demonstrate process control.

Procedure
- Prepare: Verify that the furnace is in a safe status for test activities following lockout/tagout procedures. Confirm that the control system is in a diagnostic mode that allows simulated cycles without introducing production parts to process.
- Sensor verification: Inspect signal cables and connectors to ensure secure connections and no visible damage. Exercise each sensor by simulating the condition it detects and observe the control input. Record the observed response timing using the calibration test instrument. The purpose is to detect sensor delays or intermittent signals that could add latency to the quench event.
- Timing path trace: Trace the control path from sensor input through control logic to the quench actuator. Use the calibration test instrument to capture timestamps at key points: sensor out, controller output, and actuator actuation. The rationale is to isolate which element contributes most to total delay and to provide evidence when adjustments or repairs are needed.
- Actuator check and lubrication: Verify mechanical freedom of motion for the quench actuator and linkage. If friction or stiffness is observed, apply the approved lubricant part number CFW-LUB-159 to the specified lubrication points. Operate the actuator through its cycle and measure response time to confirm improvement. Record before-and-after timing values to demonstrate effectiveness.
- Control logic verification: Place the control system into a test mode that permits single-step or simulated events. Command a simulated quench event and capture the elapsed time from command issuance to physical actuator response. Compare the measured elapsed time to the allowable maximum. The purpose is to verify that logic sequencing and communications do not introduce excess delay.
- Repeatability checks: Perform multiple simulated quench events to assess repeatability of response timing. The intent is to identify intermittent delays that could be masked by a single successful test.
- Post-test restoration: Return control system to normal operating mode, remove test instrumentation, and re-secure any access points opened for testing. Ensure lubrication points are properly cleaned and excess lubricant removed.

Acceptance criteria
- Timing performance: The measured total elapsed time from control command to physical quench actuation must be at or below the quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03), which is 13 seconds. Scope
This document defines the preventative maintenance, calibration, and verification tasks required to maintain the Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3, identified as EQ-P1-L4-HT03, in a condition that ensures process control and product conformance. The scope covers austenitizing controls, thermocouple calibration, control loop checks, door seals, atmosphere control verification, and recordkeeping required by plant quality and safety programs. Related documents include ECN-2026-002, SB-1006, and SOP-P1-L4-02 and must be consulted for change notices, safety bulletins, and operating procedures.

Background and rationale
The furnace is used for critical heat treat cycles where core microstructure and mechanical properties are sensitive to temperature uniformity and setpoint accuracy. The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C. Maintaining accurate temperature measurement and control at this setpoint is essential to avoid under- or over-austenitizing, which can lead to nonconforming forgings. Thermocouple drift and control loop degradation are the most common sources of process deviation; therefore, a dedicated calibration and verification regimen is required. The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 95 days.

Tools and materials
- Calibrated reference temperature source appropriate for high-temperature thermocouple checks (refer to SB-1006 for equipment approval).  
- Portable thermocouple calibrator and cold-junction reference.  
- Replacement thermocouple elements and connectors approved for use in EQ-P1-L4-HT03.  
- Door seal inspection kit and approved gasketing materials.  
- Logbooks, electronic maintenance entry device, or CMMS entry template per SOP-P1-L4-02.  
- Personal protective equipment as required by ECN-2026-002 and plant safety rules.

Procedure
Prepare
- Review applicable process setpoints and recent furnace run history in the electronic records system. Cross-reference any recent engineering changes per ECN-2026-002 before starting work.  
- Notify production and quality leads of planned maintenance and obtain furnace lockout/tagout in accordance with plant safety procedures referenced in SB-1006

Affected records include the on-equipment calibration log, the maintenance master record MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2, and any process run sheets that reference thermocouple verification status in SOP-P2-L4-01 and SOP-P2-L4-02.

Specifics: The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 55 days. All calibration events recorded for EQ-P2-L4-HT02 must reference MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 and be cross-referenced on the daily control log used by operators under SOP-P2-L4-01. Scope

Calibration checks confirm that control signals, sensors, and timing logic operate within acceptable behavior before parts are processed. The focus for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 is on the quench timing chain and auxiliary sensors that influence quench initiation. A failure in timing or sensor drift can result in nonconforming heat treat outcomes; timely verification mitigates production risk and reduces rework. The quench delay parameter and lubrication interfaces are high priority because they directly affect part microstructure and machine reliability.

Tools

# MM-P1-L4-HT03 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Scope
This document defines the preventative maintenance, calibration, and verification tasks required to maintain the Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3, identified as EQ-P1-L4-HT03, in a condition that ensures process control and product conformance. The scope covers austenitizing controls, thermocouple calibration, control loop checks, door seals, atmosphere control verification, and recordkeeping required by plant quality and safety programs. Related documents include ECN-2026-002, SB-1006, and SOP-P1-L4-02 and must be consulted for change notices, safety bulletins, and operating procedures.

Background and rationale
The furnace is used for critical heat treat cycles where core microstructure and mechanical properties are sensitive to temperature uniformity and setpoint accuracy. The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C. Maintaining accurate temperature measurement and control at this setpoint is essential to avoid under- or over-austenitizing, which can lead to nonconforming forgings. Thermocouple drift and control loop degradation are the most common sources of process deviation; therefore, a dedicated calibration and verification regimen is required. The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 95 days.

Tools and materials
- Calibrated reference temperature source appropriate for high-temperature thermocouple checks (refer to SB-1006 for equipment approval).  
- Portable thermocouple calibrator and cold-junction reference.  
- Replacement thermocouple elements and connectors approved for use in EQ-P1-L4-HT03.  
- Door seal inspection kit and approved gasketing materials.  
- Logbooks, electronic maintenance entry device, or CMMS entry template per SOP-P1-L4-02.  
- Personal protective equipment as required by ECN-2026-002 and plant safety rules.

Procedure
Prepare
- Review applicable process setpoints and recent furnace run history in the electronic records system. Cross-reference any recent engineering changes per ECN-2026-002 before starting work.  
- Notify production and quality leads of planned maintenance and obtain furnace lockout/tagout in accordance with plant safety procedures referenced in SB-1006

# MM-P3-L4-RR01 Maintenance manual - Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1

Plant: P3, line P3-L4

Scope
This manual provides maintenance instructions and acceptance criteria for the Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) installed on line P3-L4. It covers preventive lubrication, clamp bolt torque verification, bearings inspection, and record keeping required to support safe, repeatable operation in the heat treat cell. This document aligns with shop best practices and references related procedural documents (SB-1028, SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-03).

Background and rationale
Radial ring rolling mills in heat treat service are subject to cyclic loading, elevated ambient conditions near furnaces, and contamination from scale and quench media. Critical interfaces include the mandrel clamp and main roll bearings. The mandrel clamp bolt preload directly affects ring control and concentricity during rolling; loss of preload can produce out-of-tolerance parts and pose safety risks. Main roll bearings require a consistent lubrication cadence to preserve film thickness and prevent premature fatigue. Prescribed torque and lubrication intervals are set to maintain preload and bearing life while accommodating the mill's operating environment.

Tools
- Calibrated torque wrench capable of applying the required clamp bolt torque as specified below, with current calibration certificate referenced in maintenance records.
- Clean, lint-free rags and approved bearing-grade grease compatible with the bearing manufacturer recommendations and SOP-P3-L4-02.
- Low-pressure grease gun compatible with the mill grease fittings.
- Inspection lamp and borescope for visual assessment of bearing seals and mandrel surfaces.
- Personal protective equipment as required by SOP-P3-L4-03 and SB-1028, including heat-resistant gloves and eye protection.
- Maintenance log forms and electronic entry device for records retention.

Critical values
- The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m.
- The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 160 hours.

Mandrel clamp bolt torque verification and adjustment
- Remove any protective covers to access the mandrel clamp bolts. Clean the bolt heads and threads of debris and old lubricant following methods in SOP-P2-L4-03.
- Using the calibrated torque wrench, set the wrench to 525 N·m. Slowly apply torque to each mandrel clamp bolt until the wrench indicates the specified value. Apply torque in an alternating pattern around the mandrel to attain even clamp loading; the alternating approach prevents eccentric clamp loading and ensures uniform mandrel contact.
- After initial tightening, rotate the mandrel slowly by hand and check clamp engagement. If there is evidence of clamp slippage or rotation relative to the mandrel, repeat the torque application sequence.
- Rationale: Specifying a consistent torque reduces variability between maintenance crews and prevents under- or over-clamping which can lead to product defects or bolt fatigue.

Main roll bearing lubrication
- Confirm machine is at rest and bearings are at ambient conditions. Wipe grease fittings clean before attaching the grease gun to prevent contamination.
- Apply grease using the bearing grease gun until fresh grease is observed at the seal or purge point, taking care not to introduce contaminants. Record the lubrication event in the maintenance log with machine runtime at the time of service.
- The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is 195 hours. Schedule the next lubrication based on accumulated runtime and verify during shift handover.
- Rationale: Lubrication at the prescribed interval ensures a protective film is maintained on bearing surfaces. Over-greasing can be as damaging as under-greasing; follow the purge indicator or manufacturer guidance during application.

Bearing and roll condition inspection
- Perform a visual inspection for leaks, seal integrity, and abnormal wear on roll journals and housings. Use a dial indicator to measure runout; document readings and compare to prior records for trend detection.
- Perform a vibration scan during a light run if conditions allow (follow SOP-P2-L4-02 for restart checks). Compare spectrum signatures to baseline trends to identify bearing degradation early.
- Rationale: Trend monitoring allows maintenance to be scheduled proactively and avoids unplanned shutdowns.
